speakers: Nicolai Tangen (CEO, Norges Bank Investment Management, interviewer)
summary: Podcast with Elliott founder Paul Singer on activist investing, absolute-return risk culture and capital preservation. Covers lessons from bad trades (Japanese linkers, bankruptcy claims, Argentina holdout litigation) and a bearish view on leverage, deficits, AI valuations and crypto versus the dollar.

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: taking a position largely in an equity security of a company um and trying to um engage with the company to uh improve outcomes
claims.claim: Activist investing takes an equity position and engages the company on management, capital structure, finance strategy or asset deployment to unlock value.
claims.testable: partly - activist campaign returns are testable from 13D filings

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: index investing now accounts for a plurality of money uh money that's managed particularly Equity money
claims.claim: The shift to index investing means fewer owners scrutinize companies, which creates the room for activists to push change.
claims.testable: partly - passive share data are available

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: a consequence parenthetically of uh the trend towards index investing is that there's less coverage research coverage from Wall Street
claims.claim: As index investing grows, Wall Street research coverage declines, so firms that do their own primary research become better informed.
claims.testable: partly - analyst coverage counts are measurable

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: we develop a set of questions different from every uh in every industry and run down the questions uh we talk to a lot of people former employees uh uh customers uh Wall Street analysts
claims.claim: Elliott's research process is iterative: build an industry-specific list of questions and answer them through former employees, customers and analysts.

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: we don't get involved with highly successful companies that can't be improved really
claims.claim: Target selection focuses on companies whose boards and management are failing on strategy; Elliott studies why they are failing and avoids successful firms with no room to improve.

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: the perfect situation is a u company and this exists um you may be surprised to hear it but uh it exists a company which has an open door
claims.claim: The ideal activist target has an open door: a long-standing structure held by a founder or family out of loyalty, where part of the board or management already agrees with the change.
claims.conditions: company with entrenched legacy strategy and receptive leadership

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: everyone almost everyone sorry picks up the phone the advisers all tell them Elliot you should pick up the phone
claims.claim: Companies nearly always engage with Elliott because advisers tell them to hear out a large, credible deal-making investor, so few resist outright.

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: we have the wherewithal to to back our uh thesis and pursue our approach
claims.claim: Scale of a single large fund (about 72 billion) gives the capital and legal capacity to back a thesis and make engagement credible.

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: we have a goal we have a thesis if our thesis is right and the company takes steps
claims.claim: Elliott acts as a dealmaker with a specific thesis and goal rather than a crusader, and getting all requests is not the dominant outcome.

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: which stiff arm us and knock down drag out proxy fights or lengthy litigations doesn't really help anybody
claims.claim: Only a minority of targets resist with proxy fights or litigation, which are costly for everyone, and the usual outcome is a negotiated outcome.
claims.testable: partly - frequency of proxy fights is measurable

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: we get a meaningful percentage of what we asked for and the stock reflects it not just in 20 minutes but I mean you know over a period of time
claims.claim: Success is defined as winning a meaningful share of the requests and the stock price reflecting the added value over time, not just a short pop.

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: it's not short-termism when the market instantly overnight or in a couple of days or a few days understands
claims.claim: When an activist's plan adds long-term enterprise value, the market recognizes it within days, so a quick price reaction is not evidence of short-termism.
claims.direction: price rises on credible value-adding plan
claims.testable: yes - event study around campaign disclosure

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: this is just a guess but it's a majority it's like 70%
claims.claim: Singer guesses that value is added in nearly all cases, but only about 70% of cases lead to actual changes in structure, capital structure or directors.
claims.testable: yes - hit rates measurable from campaign data

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: fewer and fewer literally fewer and fewer people are um acting like owners yeah and fewer and fewer companies are accepting the notion that the owners have anything to say
claims.claim: Fewer shareholders act as owners and fewer companies accept owner input, which makes accountability-demanding investors rare and gives them an edge.

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: we are an absolute return fund which means that you want to make money whatever the market does
claims.claim: Elliott is an absolute return fund whose clients (universities, hospitals, charities) need performance in seriously adverse markets, not an activist-only vehicle.

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: more frequently it's we missed something we missed uh or or the hedges weren't um they weren't the right Hedges
claims.claim: Losing trades usually come from a missed risk or from hedges with more tracking error than expected, not mere bad luck.
claims.testable: yes - hedge effectiveness can be measured

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: we were long a convertible Bond and short the stock into which the convertible was convertible
claims.claim: In 1977-87 convertible arbitrage hedging was simple (long convert, short stock) with little tracking error, whereas modern trades need bespoke hedges that still fail at times.
claims.testable: yes - convertible arbitrage returns are testable

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: we've become um much more sophisticated in uh hedging in creating bespoke Hedges
claims.claim: Hedging has become more sophisticated, with bespoke hedges per trade, though even these do not work out every time.

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: the worst trades are the trades that you U misunderstand the risk you you put it into the wrong category
claims.claim: The worst trades are those where the risk is misunderstood and the position is put in the wrong category.

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: it wasn't late stage there were important bankruptcy elements that hadn't been settled
claims.claim: Buying a supposedly late-stage bankruptcy claim that was not actually late stage and whose business did not work caused a loss, showing the need to verify stage and risk category.

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: the price was minus 2% inflation per year for 7 years
claims.claim: A Japanese inflation-linked bond versus JGB arbitrage looked perfect because linkers priced about 2% annual deflation for 7 years while CPI had hovered around zero for decades.
claims.indicator: Japanese inflation-linked JGB breakeven vs CPI
claims.conditions: before 2008, when Japanese CPI stayed near zero
claims.testable: yes - breakeven vs realized CPI is observable

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: these things are Mark to Market every day
claims.claim: The linker fell about 30% as implied inflation dropped to -4.5% per year, and daily mark-to-market with leverage means a convergent trade with maturity six years out can still destroy capital and force sell-outs.
claims.testable: yes - drawdown path of arbitrage is measurable

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: when you misunderstand the risk and lever something up that you never should have levered up that way
claims.claim: Leveraging a position whose essential characteristic is misunderstood produces devastating losses, so leverage should depend on correct risk understanding.
claims.testable: partly - leverage vs loss is testable

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: where I was long stocks that I was certain because of my intellect uh i' done the research um I certain they would go up and I held them on margin
claims.claim: Concentrated conviction positions held on margin produced an 88% loss in the 1974 bear market, which shaped a no-large-loss philosophy.

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: very under underserviced uh you know High standstill rate of return um no real no really good uh valuation models
claims.claim: Convertible hedging was attractive early because it was under-serviced, offered a steady high rate of return and had no good valuation models, so edge came from relationships and fast pricing.

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: when people have losses meaningful losses they tend to lose their minds they tend to lose their judgments
claims.claim: Meaningful losses impair judgment, so protecting capital protects decision quality.
claims.testable: partly - behavior after drawdowns is studied

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: if you could keep your not only your head and your judgment intact but your Capital intact these rare periods of time when there are special opportunities
claims.claim: Keeping capital intact lets an investor exploit rare dislocations such as the last weeks of 2008 when everything got cheap before collapsing.

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: the capital is like a ratchet effect you make a buck you keep it you try to make another one
claims.claim: Capital preservation works like a ratchet: gains are kept and never given back, so compounding relies on avoiding large losses.

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: we don't Benchmark ourselves it's it's what I just told you it's don't lose money and whatever's left hopefully it's a rate of return
claims.claim: Elliott uses no benchmark; the objective is not losing money first and return second.

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: and you can't predict markets so that's that's another a dominant uh cause of me seeking never to lose money because if I want to be risk averse I have to be risk averse all the time
claims.claim: Because markets cannot be predicted, risk aversion must be constant rather than switched on and off.

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: the layer of understanding Beyond um the spreadsheet and the horrible lawyers telling you you have a 95% chance of winning that antitrust
claims.claim: Experience adds judgment beyond models and legal-probability estimates, which can be badly wrong in event-driven situations.

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: we also knew that they were coming out of World War II I think the seventh maybe the eighth largest economy in the world so you know lots of resources lots of capacity
claims.claim: Elliott bought Argentine performing bonds trading in the 70s to 80s because the country had resources and capacity and had defaulted only 3 or 4 times in 150 years, but the bonds collapsed after default.
claims.conditions: sovereign with large economy and resources
claims.testable: partly - sovereign default recovery data are available

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: a 30 Cent recovery deal for Sovereign restructuring is a number that might be appropriate for a Guatemala or a Honduras
claims.claim: Sovereign restructuring recoveries depend on a country's actual resources; a 30-cent offer fits poor countries with nothing, not a large economy like Argentina.
claims.testable: yes - recovery rates by sovereign can be compared

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: 25% of the holders held out the country said um if you don't um if you don't um uh accept this offer
claims.claim: Argentina's restructuring offers were accepted by about 75% of holders while holdouts were told they would get nothing; a creditor holding out and litigating can eventually recover more.
claims.testable: partly - holdout outcomes can be studied

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: they never accepted our offer to negotiate with them they never put a deal on the table
claims.claim: The Argentine case took 15 years because the sovereign never negotiated; the time was not patience but having no alternative since the position was already deeply underwater.

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: the long period of time um since the last major Market event has led people into thinking that they'll always be bailed out that there'll never be another uh bare Market
claims.claim: A long time since the last major market event breeds complacency, rising leverage and risk-taking, making markets as risky as Singer has seen.

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: this nerp the negative interest rate policy in uh Europe and Japan and Switzerland um um and zerp for U uh what 10 years in the US it's crazy
claims.claim: Long-lived negative and zero interest rate policy encouraged excessive leverage in governments and markets.

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: this year this fiscal year over 6% uh in the US 6% um of GDP uh deficits
claims.claim: US deficits above 6% of GDP in a non-recession year, on top of pandemic spending, are a source of fiscal risk.

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: valuations this this AI is way over its skis in terms of uh um practical um value um um being brought to users
claims.claim: Valuations around AI exceed the practical value so far delivered to users, though uses will grow.
claims.testable: partly - valuation vs earnings can be tracked

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: if governments are supporting or endorsing cryptos it's an alternative to the dollar as the reserve currency
claims.claim: Government support for crypto creates an alternative to sovereign money and thus to the dollar's reserve currency role, which other countries may welcome.

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: countries around the world are uh as you know um uh not happy with the privilege that the uh US Government um uh asserts as the central bank as the reserve currency country of the world
claims.claim: Many countries resent the privilege of the US as the reserve currency issuer and would like alternatives.

claims.speaker: Paul Singer
claims.quote: if you if you specialize uh uh too U too soon you get you get this narrow deep skill set and you're not equipped for the things that are actually happening in the world
claims.claim: Early specialization gives a narrow skill set poorly equipped for real-world events, so breadth in history, politics and philosophy is valuable for investing.
